sample_unit: responses (30 physician, 13 LLM system) to a standardized PAD case
models_evaluated: 13 LLM systems (10 standard, 3 chain-of-thought); specific names not reported in text

links.outcome: LLM adherence to 2024 ACC/AHA PAD guideline versus physicians, scored by three experts
links.effect: Adherence did not differ (physicians median 5.8 vs LLMs 7.3, p=0.169); CoT-LLMs highest (9.7). LLMs more often recommended supervised exercise (84.6% vs 30.0%) and revascularization for quality of life (69.2% vs 20.0%).
links.quote: LLM showed comparable guideline adherence to physicians although CoT models achieved the highest scores.

unlisted_practices: Chain-of-thought reasoning LLMs versus standard LLMs for guideline adherence in clinical recommendations

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the performance (guideline adherence and readability) of standard and chain-of-thought LLMs versus human specialists on a simulated clinical case of peripheral artery disease.
